newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to begin mass production of new missiles - TV.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to begin mass production of new missiles - TV.

text.p: Taiwan plans to begin mass production of a new generation of home-grown missiles to enhance its defences in the face of rival China's military threats, state television said on Thursday.
The Sky Sword II, a medium-range air-to-air missile, was designed in Taiwan to arm the island's Indigenous Defence Fighter warplane, the broadcast said.
"We can enter formal production," an official at the state-run Chungshan Institute of Science and Technology, Taiwan's main weapons research centre, told the broadcast.
The official confirmed a local newspaper report that the military planned to use the advanced radar-guided missile as the main weapon on the warplane.
"(The missile's) capability has been recognised by the air force...we can indeed enter mass production once the order is given," the official said.
He did not say how many Sky Sword II missiles the institute planned to produce or when production was scheduled to begin.
Since the 1980s, the institute has developed first- and second-generation versions of anti-ship Hsiung Feng missiles, and anti-aircraft Sky Bow and Sky Sword missiles.

Taiwan began developing advanced weapons after the United States and other supporters switched diplomatic ties to Beijing, which has increased pressure on China's diplomatic partners to stop arming what Beijing regards as a renegade province.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since the Nationalist Republic of China government lost a civil war to the communists and fled into exile to Taiwan in 1949.
China strongly objects to military links between the island and foreign countries and has vowed to attack the island if it strays from its reunification course and opts for independence.

China staged a series of war games and missile tests near Taiwan before the island's first direct presidential election last March in what Beijing acknowledged was a bid to warn Taiwan voters not to drop a state pledge to reunite with the mainland.
